summary: Mount Rainier NP summit cabin dated to the 1930s; sources split on abandonment in the 1950s versus removal in the 1960s-70s, and only concrete footings remain.

facts.design: Two-story, 14x14 cab with hip roof and encircling balconies, built by a Seattle company (per Willhite)
facts.status_note: Gone. The register and firelookout.com say abandoned in the 1950s; the NPS history and Willhite put removal in the 1960s or 1970s. Only concrete footings remain.

access.note: Inside Mount Rainier National Park, reached on foot. Willhite gives the hike as 4 miles with 3,500 feet of elevation gain.

visit.trail_note: No structure stands to climb. Willhite gives the hike as 4 miles with 3,500 feet of elevation gain; nothing remains but concrete footings, and a phone insulator survives on a small tree near the trail after the Crystal Creek crossing.

events.note: Willhite says built in 1934 under the same park construction contract as Tolmie Peak, Mount Fremont and Gobblers Knob. The register gives only 1930s.
A 2018 correspondent's recollection, printed by Willhite, says a park road crew placed dynamite in the foundation in 1974. Single unverified account.
Registered April 3, 2020 as FFLOS US 1969, WA 468

corrections.why: The FFLOS Built field reads 1930's, a decade rather than a year, and Willhite dates the cabin to 1934 under a park construction contract. Neither source gives 1930. A human should choose between 1934 (Willhite) and the 1930s (register).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give the 1930s; Willhite gives 1934. Not resolved; the story gives both.
The register and firelookout.com say the cabin was abandoned in the 1950s; the NPS history and Willhite place its removal in the 1960s or 1970s. Not resolved; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Record built year 1930 is not in any source: the FFLOS Built field reads 1930's and Willhite gives 1934 (see corrections). The end date conflicts: the register and firelookout.com say abandoned in the 1950s; the NPS history and Willhite say removed in the 1960s or 1970s. The 1974 dynamite account is one 2018 correspondent's recollection printed on Willhite's page; the road crew member is not named in the story. Fires and staffing: none in sources read. Access 'public' rests on national park status and the Willhite hike description. Firelookout.com calls the site Crystal Lake and Willhite also uses Crystal Point; the story names both. Used 5 page reads (2 of them grep reads: NPS and weebly), 1 WebSearch, and the firelookout.org list as already cached from the Crystal Mountain research.
